summary: Lane County, OR lookout: 1933 CCC tower, R-6 replacement 1962, torn down by 1982; frame reportedly moved to Warner Ridge in 1986 (sources disagree); original summit today undocumented.

facts.design: R-6 flat cab on a treated timber tower (1962); earlier 40-ft wooden 7x7 tower with ground cabin (1933)
facts.status_note: Original summit tower torn down by 1982. Sources differ on whether its frame moved to Warner Ridge in 1986 or a move failed and salvaged parts built the Warner Ridge tower. The Warner Ridge tower stands.

events.note: FFLOS: 40' wooden 7x7' tower and ground cabin. Eugene newspapers (Aug 1933) reported a 50-ft and then a 52-ft tower under construction by CCC crews.
Air supply drop of 61 pounds to lookout Don McChesney (June 1949, Eugene Register-Guard item)
Treated timber tower with R-6 cab replaced the 1933 ground house and tower; about 48,000 pounds hauled by mule. FFLOS gives 41 ft; Forest Lookouts gives 40 ft.
Lookout inspection survey: in good condition but not manned; Forest Service wanted to dispose of it
Forest Engineer report (Oct 1968): salvage for Logger Butte considered; decision on disposal by July 1, 1969

FFLOS and firelookout.com: tower (minus cab) moved to nearby Warner Ridge. Forest Lookouts: move attempt failed; salvaged materials used in new Warner Ridge tower. Warner Ridge page: superstructure came from Grass Mountain in 1986.
Registered December 18, 2010; nominated by Ray Kresek

corrections.why: 15.2 m (50 ft) matches the 1933 tower that newspapers reported at 50 to 52 ft, not the R-6 tower the record names. FFLOS gives the R-6 tower as 41 ft (12.5 m).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS and firelookout.com give 40 ft for the 1933 tower; 1933 Eugene newspaper items give 50 and 52 ft during construction. The story reports both; the record height is taken from the 1962 tower instead.
FFLOS gives 41 ft and Forest Lookouts gives 40 ft for the R-6 tower. The record uses 41 ft (12.5 m), the figure from the register.

notes_for_editor: The 1986 move is disputed: FFLOS and firelookout.com say the tower moved; Forest Lookouts says the move failed and salvaged parts built the Warner Ridge tower. Not resolved; both are reported. Brief height_m 15.2 is corrected to 12.5. No source describes the original summit today. The Warner Ridge lookout is a replica on a 40-ft tower (Recreation.gov); its name differs between sources (Warner Ridge Lookout vs Warner Mountain Lookout). Warner Ridge availability and rental status were not checked live. Firelookout.com's Warner page is an enthusiast site; Recreation.gov is the official rental listing.
